# Runtime errors (PHEL400-499)

These are raised while compiled code runs, not while it compiles. A code in this range means the program was well formed and the values it met were not.

| Code | Error |
|---|---|
| [PHEL400](#phel400-value-is-not-callable-at-runtime) | Value is not callable at runtime |
| [PHEL401](#phel401-wrong-number-of-arguments-at-runtime) | Wrong number of arguments at runtime |
| [PHEL402](#phel402-wrong-type-at-runtime) | Wrong type at runtime |
| [PHEL403](#phel403-index-out-of-bounds) | Index out of bounds |
| [PHEL404](#phel404-division-by-zero) | Division by zero |

## PHEL400: Value is not callable at runtime

Enum case: `ErrorCode::RUNTIME_NOT_CALLABLE`

A call reached a value that is not a function, and the analyzer could not see it coming. It fires when the head of the list is a name or an expression rather than a literal.

```phel
(def x 1)
(x 2)
```

**Fix:** Call a function, or read the value with an accessor such as `get`, `nth` or `first`.

## PHEL401: Wrong number of arguments at runtime

Enum case: `ErrorCode::RUNTIME_ARITY_ERROR`

A function was called with an argument count its signature does not accept. PHP raises it when the callee is a value the analyzer has no arity for, such as a local closure.

```phel
((fn [a] a))
```

**Fix:** Pass one argument per declared parameter.

## PHEL402: Wrong type at runtime

Enum case: `ErrorCode::RUNTIME_TYPE_ERROR`

A PHP function or method got an argument of a type it does not accept. Most of these come from `php/` interop calls.

```phel
(php/array_sum "x")
```

**Fix:** Convert the value to the type the callee declares before passing it.

## PHEL403: Index out of bounds

Enum case: `ErrorCode::INDEX_OUT_OF_BOUNDS`

An indexed read asked for a position the collection does not have. `nth` throws here; `get` returns `nil` instead.

```phel
(nth [1 2] 9)
```

**Fix:** Check the index against `(count coll)`, or use `get` with a default.

## PHEL404: Division by zero

Enum case: `ErrorCode::DIVISION_BY_ZERO`

A division or remainder had zero on the right. `/`, `%`, `rem` and `php/intdiv` all raise it.

```phel
(/ 1 0)
```

**Fix:** Guard the divisor before dividing.
